context:
Use the bundled schema set named by the input: set-1.json. Its tools, in file order, are:
- name "find_slots", description "Finds open meeting slots across every invited calendar, skipping holidays and any blocked focus time. Results are sorted by start time."
- name "merge_contacts", description "Merges duplicate contacts that share one email address or phone number, then keeps the newest entry. Older entries are archived, not deleted."
- name "add_days", description "Adds days to a date, e.g. weekends."
- name "pick_source", description "Uses e.g. The calendar feed. Falls back to local time."
- name "ping_service", description "Checks that the service is up and answering"
- name "ask_user", description "Asks the user a question? Waits for the reply! Then returns it. Times out after a minute."
- name "export_notes", description "Exports notes as Markdown.\n\n  Each note becomes one file."
- name "Export_notes", description "  Exports   notes as plain\ttext,\none file per folder."
- name "log_event", description ""
- name "clear_cache", description null
- name "noop", description " \n\t "
- name "hash_blob", description "012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789 is the test vector for this hash. Others are optional."
- name "Zeta_sync", description "Syncs the zeta store. Runs nightly."
- name "alpha_sync", description "Syncs the alpha store."

Build the compact index under these rules.
1. Collapse every run of whitespace (including newlines and tabs) in each description to a single space, then trim.
2. The summary is the description's first sentence: everything up to and including the first period that is followed by a space and an uppercase letter (A to Z). If there is none, the whole collapsed description is the summary. Only periods end sentences, not ? or !. So "Adds days, e.g. weekends." stays whole, but "Uses e.g. The calendar." splits after "e.g.".
3. A summary of 100 characters or fewer is kept as is. A longer one is cut to the most whole words (space-separated pieces after rule 1) that fit in 99 characters, followed by "…" with no space, so the total is at most 100. If the first word alone is longer than 99 characters, cut it at 99 and add "…". The ellipsis is one character.
4. An empty, missing (null), or whitespace-only description gets "(no description)".
5. Entries are sorted by lowercased name; names differing only in case are ordered by their exact name (uppercase before lowercase). Two tools with exactly the same name make the set invalid; names differing only in case are distinct.
6. Each entry is "name: summary", the name exactly as written.

No other data is needed.
